headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via Khoj’s shared indexed notes; the pair lacks direct interaction evidence, so other risks stay lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj can read indexed personal notes/files and has broad network egress, so if system_prompts_leaks content is placed in the shared index or copied into a note, its instructions could be surfaced to the user. system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak corpus, so the interaction is plausible, though not directly documented here.
conditions: IF system_prompts_leaks content is ingested into Khoj's indexed notes/files
IF Khoj presents retrieved file text as instruction-like content without provenance labeling
mitigations: Exclude the leak corpus from Khoj indexing
Tag retrieved snippets as untrusted provenance
Disable automatic instruction-following from retrieved notes
Review any retrieved prompt-like text before acting on it

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, while system_prompts_leaks is a repository of prompt-leak material. If both are placed in the same shared workspace or index, sensitive notes could be exposed through retrieval or search results. The pairwise path is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF personal notes and system_prompts_leaks content share the same indexed workspace
IF retrieved snippets from the shared index are visible to users who should not access the underlying notes
mitigations: Separate the leak corpus from personal-note indexes
Restrict search results to per-user namespaces
Audit indexed sources for sensitive documents
Turn off indexing for any confidential folder

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj has read-only filesystem access and no git or shell write capability, while system_prompts_leaks is source-available and runnable:false. There is no shared write surface or overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict appears limited.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF a separate tool layer adds mutable shared state not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only mounts
Avoid shared writable workspaces
Do not grant git write permissions
Use separate service accounts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can retrieve and present indexed content, and system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about leaked prompts. If Khoj treats retrieved text as authoritative, leaked or malicious instructions could cascade into user-facing answers. No verification step is documented, so the safer severity is medium.
conditions: IF Khoj uses retrieved snippets as authoritative guidance
IF the retrieved content is not manually verified before being shown or acted on
mitigations: Require source citations on retrieved answers
Add a verification step for prompt-like content
Flag leak-corpus snippets as untrusted
Limit downstream actions from retrieved text

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents, which can include regulated data, but the profile does not show a residency or certification mismatch with system_prompts_leaks. Because the second agent is source-available and not a data processor with stated compliance claims, only a limited overlap risk is evident.
conditions: IF regulated personal notes are indexed into Khoj alongside the leak corpus
IF an operator expects a documented compliance boundary that is not present in either profile
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared index
Document data-class boundaries
Review retention settings for indexed notes
Use separate deployments for sensitive and non-sensitive content
